questions.question: Which of the following education commissions was appointed In 1882?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hunter Commission.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Hunter Commission of 1882 was presided over by Sir William Hunter.
 
• This Commission was appointed for the enquiry of education in India which was earlier given by Wood’s Despatch in 1854.
 
• Recommendations of the Hunter Commission:
 
 
• Preference was given to literate candidates for government jobs in the lower levels, along with the expansion of primary schools in backward districts.
 
• District and municipal boards were entrusted with the management of primary education under the Local Self Government Act. The funds were separated for rural and urban areas to avoid funds earmarked for rural schools being misappropriated by urban schools.
 
• Secondary schools were to be established by private parties with funds provided by the government. Model schools fully run by the government were to be opened in each district to guide such private schools.
 
• The secondary school curriculum was also revised with academic and vocational courses diversified into different branches.
 
• Missionary schools were discouraged, and Indian participation in the private school system was solicited by the raj. Special care was supposed to be taken in advancing the education of girls and women.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sadler Commission-1917

 
 
• As observed by the Sadler Commission in 1917, The next important evolution was the realization of the need for the advancement of secondary education for the enhancement of University education.
 
• This agitate also stemmed from the need for ramifying college courses.
 
• Sadler Commission suggested bifurcating higher education at the intermediate examination instead of the matriculation examination.
 
• Suggested the formation of Intermediate colleges which would provide instruction in Arts, Medicine, Science, Teaching, Engineering, etc
 
 
 
• **The Calcutta University Commission**
 
 
• In 1917, the Calcutta University Commission was appointed by the Government of India under the Chairmanship of Mr. Michel Sadler, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Leeds.
 
• So it was popularly known as the Sadler Commission. This Commission was appointed for the purpose of making recommendations to reform Calcutta University.
 
• Although it dealt with Calcutta University only, the problems it studied were more or less common to other Indian Universities.
 
• Hence, the report of the Commission is a document of provincial importance and it had far-reaching consequences on the development of universities in India as a whole.
 
 
 
• **The University Commission**
 
 
• **Lord Curzon** evinced a keen interest in the development of education in British India.
 
• Soon after his arrival as Viceroy, he convened one educational conference at Shimla in 1901, to discuss the problems ranging from Primary to University education.
 
• A University Commission was appointed on January 27, 1902.

questions.question: What proportion of the proposed jobs has been reserved for women as per the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one third.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):

__
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was enacted by the Central Government of India in the year 2005.
 
• It mandates that **women** must receive priority in order for them to make up **at least one-third of the beneficiaries.**
 
• Established by the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• MGNREGA is one of the biggest labor guarantee programs globally.
 
• The main goal of the program is to provide adult members of rural households who are willing to perform unskilled manual labor related to public work with 100 days of employment guaranteed per fiscal year.
 
• The legally-backed guarantee that any adult living in a rural area would find a job within 15 days of requesting it, or else an "unemployment allowance" must be provided, is the most significant aspect of the MGNREGA framework.
 
• By giving women equal pay for equal labour, MGNREGA has been successful in lowering poverty, raising the standard of living in rural households, and empowering them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Right to Work:

 
• It is not specifically acknowledged as a fundamental right in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is unenforceable in a court of law because it is included in Part IV of the Constitution (Directive Principles of State Policy) under Article 41.
 
• According to Article 41 of the Constitution, “the State shall within the limits of its economic capacity and development, make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.”

questions.question: In which year was the Citizenship Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Citizenship Act was first passed in India in the year **1955.**
 
• **The original Citizenship Act of 1955 **laid down the framework for Indian citizenship and defined the various ways in which a person could acquire or lose citizenship in India.
 
• Since its enactment, the act has undergone several amendments to accommodate changes and evolving perspectives on citizenship. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are four main ways through which an individual can acquire Indian citizenship:
 
 
• **By Birth:** A person born in India on or after January 26, 1950, is considered an Indian citizen by birth, with a few exceptions.
 
• **By Descent:** Individuals born outside India on or after January 26, 1950, but have at least one Indian parent, are eligible for Indian citizenship by descent.
 
• **By Registration: **Certain categories of people, such as individuals of Indian origin residing outside India, can acquire Indian citizenship through registration by fulfilling specific criteria.
 
• **By Naturalization:** Foreigners who have resided in India for a specified period of time and meet other qualifications can apply for Indian citizenship through naturalization.

questions.question: What is the main objective of Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA), 2003?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reduce fiscal deficit**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main objective of the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA), 2003** is to **reduce the fiscal deficit** of the government.
 
• The act aims to ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management and long-term macroeconomic stability.
 
• It provides a legal institutional framework for reducing the fiscal deficit and improving fiscal discipline.
 
• FRBMA mandates the government to present to the Parliament a medium-term fiscal policy statement, a fiscal policy strategy statement, and a macro-economic framework statement annually along with the budget.
 
• The act also sets targets for reducing government debt and maintaining prudent levels of public spending and borrowing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The FRBMA was enacted by the Parliament of India in August 2003.
 
• The act was amended in 2018 to replace the fiscal deficit targets with a fiscal roadmap and to introduce a debt-to-GDP ratio target.
 
• According to the act, the central government is required to limit the fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP by the end of a specified period.
 
• The act also aims to eliminate revenue deficit and bring down the public debt-to-GDP ratio to a sustainable level over the medium term.
 
• Effective implementation of the FRBMA is crucial for achieving fiscal consolidation and enhancing the credibility of the government's fiscal policy.

questions.question: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Parliament **passed the **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014,** which was subsequently approved by the President on **March 1, 2014**.
 
• This act, commonly referred to as the **Telangana Act,** came into effect on June 2, 2014, leading to the formation of two new states:** Telangana and the remaining part of Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The enactment of this legislation was a response to the Telangana movement, which advocated for the creation of a separate state of Telangana.
 
• As a result, the state of Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated into Telangana and the residual Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, mandates the division of assets, liabilities, employees, and contracts between the two newly formed states, ensuring a smooth transition and administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In August 2013, the **Union Cabinet** established a **Group of Ministers (GoM)** committee to assess the feasibility of dividing Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The committee was chaired by the Union Home Minister, Sushil Kumar Shinde. Other members of the committee included the Finance Minister, P. Chidambaram, the Health Minister, Ghulam Nabi Azad, the Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister, Veerappa Moily, the Union Rural Development Minister, Jairam Ramesh, and the Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Narayanaswamy.
 
• The committee's objective was to examine various aspects of the potential division, drawing insights from the findings of the Srikrishna committee on Telangana.

questions.question: As per the Hindu Succession Act 1956, who amongst the following has the first right over the property of a Hindu woman who dies intestate?

options.text: The legal heirs of her husband
The legal heirs of her father

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Her husband.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **As per the Hindu Succession Act 1956, Her husband has the first right over the property of a Hindu woman who dies intestate.**
 
• The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 (39 of 2005) was enacted to remove gender discriminatory provisions in the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
 
• Under the amendment, the daughter of a coparcener shall by birth become a coparcener in her own right in the same manner as the son.
 
• The daughter shall now have the same rights in the coparcenary property (ancestral property of the Hindu undivided family) as a son.
 
• This amendment also repeals Section 23 of the Hindu Succession Act which disentitled a female heir to ask for partition in respect of a dwelling house, wholly occupied by a joint family, until the male heirs choose to divide their respective shares.
 
• Section 24 of the Act which denied the rights of a widow to inherit her husband's property upon her re-marriage has been repealed.
 
• This Act has brought about a central amendment that is applicable to all state governments.

questions.question: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the ________ to establish authorities charged with the mandate of preventing environmental pollution in all its forms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, is an Act of the Parliament of India, enacted in the wake of the Bhopal Gas Tragedy.
 
• The Act empowers the Central Government to make rules to regulate environmental pollution and to establish authorities for the purpose.
 
• It provides the Central Government with the authority to take all necessary measures to protect and improve the quality of the environment.
 
• It encompasses a wide range of regulations and standards to control pollution and manage hazardous substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**

 
 
• The Act was passed in response to the need for overarching legislation to protect and improve the environment.
 
• The Act gives the Central Government the power to take measures for environmental protection, such as setting standards for emissions or discharge of environmental pollutants from various sources.
 
• It provides a framework for coordinating the activities of various central and state authorities established under other laws to ensure environmental protection.
 
• The Act also includes provisions for penalties for contravention of the standards and restrictions set by the government.
 
 
 
• **Key Provisions of the Act**
 
 
• **Section 3:** Empowers the Central Government to take measures to protect and improve the environment and to prevent, control, and abate environmental pollution.
 
• **Section 6:** Empowers the Central Government to make rules to regulate environmental pollution, including standards for the quality of the environment, and the maximum allowable concentrations of various pollutants.
 
• **Section 15:** Provides for penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of the Act, including imprisonment and fines.
 
• **Section 19:** Allows any person to file a complaint in a court of law against anyone who fails to comply with the Act's provisions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Act**
 
 
• The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, serves as a comprehensive framework for the protection and improvement of the environment in India.
 
• It addresses the need for a unified approach to environmental regulation and management.
 
• The Act empowers the government to take proactive measures to prevent environmental degradation and to respond effectively to environmental emergencies.
 
• It plays a crucial role in ensuring sustainable development and safeguarding public health and well-being.

questions.question: In relation to the state of Tamil Nadu, the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2022 will include the __________ and Kurivikkaran communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes in Tamil Nadu.

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2022 includes the **Narikoravan** and Kurivikkaran communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The inclusion of these communities aims to provide them with the benefits and protections available to Scheduled Tribes under the Constitution of India.
 
• This amendment is part of the ongoing efforts to recognize and support the diverse tribal communities in the country.
 
• Scheduled Tribes are provided with various affirmative action measures including reservations in education, employment, and political representation to ensure their development and integration into mainstream society.

• The inclusion of a community in the Scheduled Tribes list allows its members to avail various constitutional safeguards and welfare measures aimed at their socio-economic upliftment.

questions.question: Which Act was enacted by the British which regulated the manufacture, sale, possession and transport of firearms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Arms Act, 1878**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Arms Act, 1878** was enacted by the **British to regulate the manufacture, sale, possession, and transport of firearms**.
 
• This Act was part of the colonial measures to **control arms and ammunition **among the Indian population.
 
• The Act required that Indians obtain licenses to possess, sell, or manufacture arms and ammunition.
 
• It was** aimed at preventing any potential uprising** or revolt by restricting access to weapons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian Arms Act, 1878** was one of several laws enacted to maintain British control over India.
 
• The Act was repealed and replaced by the **Arms Act of 1959** post-Independence, which governs the current regulations related to arms and ammunition in India.
 
• The Arms Act of 1959 aims to curb illegal arms and ensure that firearms are used responsibly.
 
• Licenses for arms are now issued under the provisions of the 1959 Act, which includes various checks and balances to prevent misuse.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts prevents disrespect to the National Flag and National Anthem?

options.text: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act of 1971** serves to safeguard the integrity of the **National Flag, National Anthem, and Constitution of India. **This legislation imposes penalties on individuals who display disrespect towards these national symbols.
 
• Offenders can face imprisonment for up to three years, a monetary fine, or both. The Act also regulates the proper hoisting, usage, and exhibition of the Indian National Flag.
 
• Among its provisions are prohibitions against allowing the flag to touch the ground or be draped over vehicles, buildings, or other objects. Additionally, intentional display of the flag with the saffron color facing downwards is deemed inappropriate.
 
• The Supreme Court has clarified that respectful standing during the National Anthem, even if not sung, does not constitute a violation of the Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Part IVA of the Indian Constitution** outlines the fundamental duties of Indian citizens, which include adhering to the Constitution, respecting its principles and institutions, as well as honoring the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• The corresponding Act elaborates on the penalties for contravening Article 51Aa of the Constitution.
 
• According to this Act, individuals holding high-ranking positions such as the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and other government officials can face disqualification if found guilty of violating the Constitution, as per sections 7 and 8(k) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
• In instances where the judiciary annuls unconstitutional actions of the executive, these actions are deemed as written acts visible to the public, thereby constituting contempt of the Constitution of India or its provisions.

questions.question: In _____, the Indian Parliament passed the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA).

The correct answer is December 2019.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA)** was **passed **by the Indian Parliament on **December 11, 2019.**
 
• The **Citizenship Amendment Bill (CAA Bill)** was **first introduced in 2016 in Lok Sabha** for amending the Citizenship Act of 1955.
 
 
• A Joint Parliamentary Committee was tasked with reviewing this bill; the committee eventually turned in its findings on January 7, 2019.
 
• On January 8, 2019, the Lok Sabha enacted the Citizenship Amendment Bill, which expired on the same day as the 16th Lok Sabha was dissolved. 
 
 
 
• Amit Shah, the Minister of Home Affairs,** reintroduced** this bill in the **17th Lok Sabha on December 9, 2019**, and it was subsequently **passed in that house on December 10.**
 
 
• On **December 11**, the **Rajya Sabha also approved** the measure. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) 2019:**
 
• It **amends **the **Citizenship Act of 1955** to **grant citizenship to** six non-Muslim populations (**Hindus**, **Sikhs**, **Buddhists**, **Jains**, **Parsis**, and **Christians**) who **entered India** illegally on or **before December 31, 2014**, on the basis of their faith.
 
 
• These communities **should be from Pakistan, Afghanistan, **and **Bangladesh.**
 
 
 
• Members of the six communities are **released from prosecution under** the **Passport Act of 1920** and the **Foreigners Act of 1946.**
 
• If a person has **lived in India for 11 of the preceding 14 years** and **for the last 12 months**, they are **eligible **under this statute.
 
 
• The period of residency has been shortened from 11 to 5 years for the designated class of undocumented migrants.

questions.question: Which Act allows persecution of a person who being abroad refuses to return to India to face criminal prosecution?

options.text: International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fugitive Economic Offenders (FEO) Act, 2018.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fugitive Economic Offenders (FEO) Act, 2018** allows persecution of a person who being abroad refuses to return to India to face criminal prosecution.
 
• A person is to be declared as an FEO under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 if: 
 
• an arrest warrant has been issued against him for any specified offences where the value involved is over Rs. 100 crore, and
 
• he has left the country and refuses to return to face prosecution

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• To declare a person an FEO, an application will be filed in a Special Court (designated under the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002) containing details of the properties to be confiscated. The Special Court will require the person to appear at a specified place at least six weeks from the issue of notice. Proceedings will be terminated if the person appears.
 
• Authorities can provisionally attach properties of an accused, while the application is pending before the Special Court. Upon declaration as an FEO, the properties of a person may be confiscated and vested in the central government. Further, the FEO or any company associated with him may be barred from filing or defending civil claims.

__
 
• Official Secrets Act has its roots in the British colonial era.
 
 
• The original version was the Indian Official Secrets Act (Act XIV), 1889.
 
• It was amended and made more stringent in the form of the Indian Official Secrets Act, 1904, during Lord Curzon’s tenure as Viceroy of India.
 
 
 
• In 1923, a newer version was notified.
 
 
• The Indian Official Secrets Act (Act No XIX of 1923) was extended to all matters of secrecy and confidentiality in governance in the country.
 
• It broadly deals with two aspects - spying or espionage, covered under Section 3, and disclosure of other secret information of the government, under Section 5.
 
• Secret information can be any official code, password, sketch, plan, model, article, note, document, or information.
 
 
 
• Under Section 5, both the person communicating the information and the person receiving the information can be punished. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Official Secrets Act, 1923**, extended its provisions to protect the privacy and secrecy of the governance of the country especially for the national security of the country. The Act lays down **several provisions** out of which some are:

 
 
• **Section 5** puts forth the provision of offense caused by **“wrongful communication of information.”** If someone reveals a secret official code or password or any sketch, plan, model, article, note, document or information, a prohibited place or a similar place, whose sufficient information could help a potential enemy, or a high official under a government who has been conferred with the responsibility of protecting such confidential information, or a person employed under such an official or bound by a contract or holds a contract on behalf of the government if fails to properly conduct himself and cause harm to the information held, uses such details and knowledge for helping a foreign power or in a way ‘prejudicial to the safety of the State,’ or purposefully communicates such details to someone who is not authorized is held to be guilty under this section. 
 
• **Section 4** highlights that **“foreign agent”** means any person who has reasonable grounds for being suspected as he or she is employed by a foreign power by any means, for the purpose of carrying out an act with or without compliance to the safety of the state [India], prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State, or who can be suspected for committing or trying to commit the act for the interest of the foreign power. 
 
• **Section 4(c) **further highlights that any location or address with the perfect reason of being suspected for receiving communications for an agents purpose or where a foreign agent resides, gives or receives information, or could be where he carries out any business, maybe assumed as an address of a foreign agent, and communications addressed is to be known as connecting with a foreign agent.
 
• **Under Section 6** if any person for getting entry or helping another to enter a prohibited area which goes against the safety of the state while doing so if wears an official uniform or a resembling uniform without legal authority for deceiving and representing himself to be someone with authority, or, gets an oral or written declaration or document or makes any false statements, or, deceiving someone represents himself to be an official employed by the government to receive secret and classified information, etc, is held guilty for committing an offense under this Section. **Section 6(3) **imposes imprisonment for a term of three years, or with a fine, or both for committing an offense under this section.
